sentences.en: Our observations had taught us to conceive a spectacle exceeding our original expectations,
sentences.zh: 我们的观察让我们预想到了一个远超最初预期的奇观，

sentences.en: but they had not prepared us for the extent and display of the scene which here burst upon us.
sentences.zh: 但眼前突然展现的景象之宏大与壮丽，仍令我们始料未及。

sentences.en: An area nearly a mile in circumference was crowded with magnificence and novelty.
sentences.zh: 一片周长近一英里的区域内，挤满了华丽而新奇的事物。

sentences.en: At least a hundred large umbrellas or canopies which could shelter 30 persons were sprung up and down by the bearers with brilliant effect.
sentences.zh: 至少有一百把大型遮阳伞或华盖，每把足以容纳三十人，被抬伞人上下挥动，呈现出绚丽夺目的效果。

sentences.en: The superior captains and attendants wore a shanty cloths of extravagant price.
sentences.zh: 高级船长和随从们穿着价格昂贵的棚屋布料。

sentences.en: These were of incredible size and weight and thrown over the shoulder exactly like a Roman toga.
sentences.zh: 这些布料尺寸和重量惊人，像古罗马托加长袍一样披在肩上。

sentences.en: A small silk fillet generally encircled their temples and massy gold necklaces intricately wrought suspended Moorish charMs.
sentences.zh: 他们的鬓角通常围着一条丝绸发带，沉甸甸的金项链上悬挂着工艺精湛的摩尔式护身符。

sentences.en: Gold and silver pipes and canes called the eye in every direction.
sentences.zh: 金银烟斗和手杖在各个方向都引人注目。

sentences.en: Wolves and rams' heads as large as life, cast in gold, were suspended from their gold-handled swords.
sentences.zh: 与实物大小相当的狼头和羊头金饰，悬挂在他们金柄的佩剑上。

sentences.en: So that, Tom Holland, was T.E.
sentences.zh: 所以，汤姆·霍兰德，那就是T.E.。

sentences.en: Bowditch, who was the first Englishman to leave a written account of the court of the King of Ashanti after his visit in May 1817.
sentences.zh: 鲍迪奇是第一位在1817年5月访问阿散蒂王国后，留下关于该国宫廷书面记录的英国人。

sentences.en: And we're in the middle of our great World Cup odyssey, aren't we, through the countries that have qualified for the tournament in Qatar.
sentences.zh: 我们正处于世界杯之旅的中心，不是吗？我们正在走访那些获得了卡塔尔世界杯参赛资格的国家。

sentences.en: We are talking about the Ashanti Kingdom.
sentences.zh: 我们正在谈论的是阿散蒂王国。

sentences.en: So this is the episode for, Tom?
sentences.zh: 所以这是汤姆的那一集吗？

sentences.en: For Ghana.
sentences.zh: 是关于加纳的。

sentences.en: For Ghana.
sentences.zh: 为了加纳。

sentences.en: And I will confess right away that I know genuinely nothing at all about this subject.
sentences.zh: 我得先坦白，我对这个话题确实一无所知。

sentences.en: So I'm greatly looking forward to being educated, Tom.
sentences.zh: 所以我非常期待能从你这里学到知识，汤姆。

sentences.en: Well, I'm not going to pretend that I am in any way a specialist in the study of the Ashanti Empire either.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我也不会假装自己是研究阿散蒂帝国的专家。

sentences.en: Actually, ever since I read Dan Morris' book Heaven's Command, which describes the British expeditions against this extraordinary empire in what is now Ghana, Ashanti land.
sentences.zh: 事实上，自从我读了丹·莫里斯的《天堂的命令》一书后，书中描述了英国对这个位于现今加纳阿散蒂地区的非凡帝国进行的远征。

sentences.en: And I guess the Ashanti are probably up there with the Zulus as the African empire that most impressed the British.
sentences.zh: 我想阿散蒂人大概和祖鲁人一样，是给英国人留下最深刻印象的非洲帝国。

sentences.en: And because the British tended to write the earliest reports, they're a kind of very vivid record.
sentences.zh: 而且因为英国人往往会写下最早的报告，所以它们留下了非常生动的记录。

sentences.en: Today is Ghana.
sentences.zh: 今天是加纳。

sentences.en: And as you will know, Ghana is the oldest football association in Africa, 1920.
sentences.zh: 如你所知，加纳是非洲最古老的足球协会，成立于1920年。

sentences.en: So Ghana is the coast is the gold coaSt.
sentences.zh: 所以加纳就是海岸，也就是黄金海岸。

sentences.en: And so it's a place where ever since the arrival of the Portuguese, you have the interface with Europeans.
sentences.zh: 因此，自葡萄牙人抵达以来，这里一直是一个与欧洲人交流的交汇点。

sentences.en: There is this kind of fascinating synergy.
sentences.zh: 这是一种令人着迷的协同效应。

sentences.en: And also the forest of what is now Ghana is linked to the lands further north.
sentences.zh: 而且，如今加纳境内的森林也与更北方的土地相连。

sentences.en: So the Islamic world, too.
sentences.zh: 伊斯兰世界也是如此。

sentences.en: So this is kind of through the early modern period.
sentences.zh: 所以这大致贯穿了整个近代早期。

sentences.en: There is this kind of interface between the European powers on the coast,
sentences.zh: 在海岸上的欧洲列强、

sentences.en: the Islamic civilizations to the north and the various peoples who are kind of moving in to what will become Ghana.
sentences.zh: 北方的伊斯兰文明，以及正陆续迁入未来加纳领土的各族人民之间，存在着这样一种交汇。

sentences.en: And of all these people, the Ashanti are by far the most famous.
sentences.zh: 而在所有这些民族中，阿散蒂人无疑是最出名的。

sentences.en: And in terms of building huge empires and constructing cities, the most impressive.
sentences.zh: 就建立庞大帝国和兴建城市而言，他们也是最令人印象深刻的。

sentences.en: So where did the Ashanti come from?
sentences.zh: 那么，阿散蒂人是从哪里来的呢？

sentences.en: Well, the Ashanti themselves have various traditions.
sentences.zh: 嗯，阿散蒂人自己有各种各样的传说。

sentences.en: So one of the traditions is that they fell from the sky.
sentences.zh: 其中一个传说就是他们是从天上掉下来的。

sentences.en: Another tradition is that they emerged from holes in the ground.
sentences.zh: 另一个传统说法是，他们是从地洞中走出来的。

sentences.en: And another tradition is that they emerged from a lake called Besomptwe, which James Morris describes as a sinister tree infested mere,
sentences.zh: 还有一个传统说法是，他们是从一个叫贝松普韦的湖里出来的，詹姆斯·莫里斯将其描述为一个阴森恐怖、树木丛生的湖泊。

sentences.en: which intermittently belched gas and mud from its recesses.
sentences.zh: 它不时地从深处喷出气体和泥浆。

sentences.en: And actually, the tradition is that it's not just the Ashanti who come from Lake Besomptwe, but the entire human race.
sentences.zh: 事实上，根据传统，不仅阿散蒂人来自博松特维湖，全人类也都源于此。

sentences.en: So what you get with those three traditions is the idea that the Ashanti have always been in Ghana, whether they've fallen from the sky or whether they've emerged from a lake
sentences.zh: 因此，这三种传统所传达的理念是，阿散蒂人一直都在加纳，无论他们是来自天降，还是源于湖泊，

sentences.en: or whether they've emerged from the ground.
sentences.zh: 亦或是从地底涌现。

sentences.en: And actually, one of the things that strikes me reading about the Ashanti is the kind of the trace, the echoes of Greek or Roman traditions.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在阅读关于阿散蒂人的资料时，有一点让我印象深刻，那就是他们身上似乎有着古希腊或古罗马传统的痕迹与回响。

sentences.en: I mean, obviously, they're completely coincidental, but the Athenians had this idea that what they called autochthonous, that they were sprung from the soil,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这显然纯属巧合，但雅典人曾有一种观念，他们称之为“本土起源”，认为他们是从土地中生长出来的，

sentences.en: and that this gave them a peculiar hold on the land that they lived in.
sentences.zh: 而这赋予了他们对自己所居住土地的一种独特的掌控力。

sentences.en: So that was part of the Ashanti tradition.
sentences.zh: 所以那是阿散蒂传统的一部分。

sentences.en: But there is also a tradition that they came from the Savannah to the north.
sentences.zh: 但也有另一种传统认为他们来自北方的热带稀树草原。

sentences.en: And that is obviously what's likelier than the fact that they fell from the sky or that they came from a lake, probably.
sentences.zh: 显然，这比他们从天而降或从湖中走出来的说法要靠谱得多。

sentences.en: And just to, so coming from the Savannah to the north, can you put us in time a little bit more specifically?
sentences.zh: 那么，关于从北方的稀树草原迁徙而来，你能更具体地帮我们梳理一下时间线吗？

sentences.en: So when are we talking about?
sentences.zh: 我们具体是指什么时候？

sentences.en: Probably over the course of the Middle Ages.
sentences.zh: 大概是在中世纪期间。

sentences.en: Right, that's quite a long period.
sentences.zh: 没错，那是一个相当长的时期。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, because there are no real written records about it.
sentences.zh: 是啊，毕竟关于这段历史并没有真正的文字记载。

sentences.en: The archaeology is difficult because there's rainforest everywhere.
sentences.zh: 考古工作也很困难，因为到处都是雨林。

sentences.en: So it's difficult to really say anything more certain than the fact that various peoples, various groupings are migrating into this region
sentences.zh: 所以很难说出比“各种民族和群体正在迁入该地区”更确切的结论了。

sentences.en: and indeed over the whole of, you know, all along the coast, not just into Ghana.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你知道，整个沿海地区都是如此，不仅仅是在加纳。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Over the course of the Middle Ages.
sentences.zh: 在中世纪的过程中。

sentences.en: And with the coming of the Portuguese, you start to get a degree of state building because the Portuguese are buyers for slaves and for gold.
sentences.zh: 随着葡萄牙人的到来，你开始看到一定程度的国家建设，因为葡萄牙人是奴隶和黄金的买家。

sentences.en: Yeah, yes.
sentences.zh: 没错，是的。

sentences.en: And so a kind of international process of exchange is starting to build up.
sentences.zh: 因此，一种国际性的交换进程开始建立起来。

sentences.en: And you need structures in place to be able to ship these things to the coaSt.
sentences.zh: 你需要建立相应的结构，才能把这些东西运到海岸。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And then to sell them and then to regulate their trade or whatever, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 然后把它们卖掉，再对它们的贸易进行监管之类的，我想是这样。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And so by the 17th century, there is this people, this empire called the Denkira.
sentences.zh: 到了17世纪，出现了一个民族，一个被称为登基拉的帝国。

sentences.en: And they are occupying the Gold Coast in Ghana and the kind of region inland.
sentences.zh: 他们占据了加纳的黄金海岸以及内陆地区。

sentences.en: And they are the dominant power.
sentences.zh: 他们是当时的主导力量。

sentences.en: And there are various kind of other peoples who are subordinate to them.
sentences.zh: 还有各种各样的其他民族从属于他们。

sentences.en: And among these people, other people who will become the Ashanti.
sentences.zh: 在这些人当中，有后来成为阿散蒂人的群体。

sentences.en: I'm going to call them the Ashanti throughout, but they only get to be called the Ashanti later on for a reason that we'll come to.
sentences.zh: 我打算全程称他们为阿散蒂人，但他们之所以后来才被称为阿散蒂人，是有原因的，我们稍后会讲到。

sentences.en: So by the 17th century, an Ashanti state is starting to incubate within the broader empire of the Denkira.
sentences.zh: 所以到了17世纪，一个阿散蒂国家开始在登基拉帝国的大框架内孕育。

sentences.en: And there are all kinds of stories told about this process that for anyone familiar with Greek or Roman mythology would be familiar.
sentences.zh: 关于这个过程流传着各种各样的故事，任何熟悉希腊或罗马神话的人都会感到熟悉。

sentences.en: So they talk about how their state is founded by two twins called Twum and Antwi.
sentences.zh: 他们讲述了自己的国家是如何由一对名叫特乌姆和安特维的双胞胎建立的。

sentences.en: And the kind of echoes of Romulus and Remus there are, you know, suggestive.
sentences.zh: 那种罗慕路斯与雷穆斯的传说回响，你知道，很有暗示意味。

sentences.en: Because these are, I guess, kind of primal legends.
sentences.zh: 因为我想，这些都是某种原始传说。

sentences.en: There are only so many origin stories that you can construct.
sentences.zh: 你能构建的起源故事终究有限。

sentences.en: But what's clear is that by the 17th century, a bit like the Denkira further south, the people who will become the Ashanti are starting to consolidate.
sentences.zh: 但显而易见的是，到了17世纪，就像更南边的登基拉人一样，那些后来成为阿散蒂人的人们开始整合起来了。

sentences.en: And again, it's basically, I think, because with the introduction of large quantities of iron, it's possible for them to start clearing, you know, villages.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，这基本上是因为随着大量铁器的引入，他们才有可能开始清理出村庄。

sentences.en: So you start to get this pattern of very thick jungle and open patches where the soil is kind of very red.
sentences.zh: 于是你开始看到这种模式：茂密的丛林中出现了开阔的空地，土壤呈现出一种深红色。

sentences.en: And that means that they can start to plant crops.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他们可以开始种植农作物了。

sentences.en: And this is a period in the 17th century when the produce of the Americas is starting to be introduced, and particularly maize.
sentences.zh: 这是17世纪的一个时期，美洲的农产品开始被引入，尤其是玉米。

sentences.en: And so I remember when we did our episodes on Portugal, somebody on Twitter said,
sentences.zh: 我记得当我们做关于葡萄牙的节目时，推特上有人说，

sentences.en: I hope you're going to talk about how the Portuguese introduced maize into Africa and how this became the staple crop.
sentences.zh: 我希望你们能谈谈葡萄牙人是如何将玉米引入非洲，以及它是如何成为主食的。

sentences.en: And we didn't, did we?
sentences.zh: 我们当时没讲，对吧？

sentences.en: But no, we didn't.
sentences.zh: 没错，我们没讲。

sentences.en: I mean, did you know that?
sentences.zh: 我是说，你知道那件事吗？

sentences.en: I didn't know that.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: No, I didn't.
sentences.zh: 不，我不知道。

sentences.en: I didn't know that.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: So this is our opportunity to make amends for that.
sentences.zh: 所以这是我们弥补遗憾的机会。

sentences.en: But it's, it's not, so it's not just maize that's being introduced.
sentences.zh: 但不仅仅是玉米被引入了。

sentences.en: It's avocados, tomatoes, pineapples, oranges, all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 还有鳄梨、西红柿、菠萝、橙子，诸如此类的东西。

sentences.en: They come from the Americas.
sentences.zh: 它们都来自美洲。

sentences.en: I didn't know that, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这一点，汤姆。

sentences.en: Well, this is an education, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 好吧，多米尼克，这真是一次学习。

sentences.en: But you will know that, of course, that the other thing is, is the gold.
sentences.zh: 但你当然会知道，另一件事是黄金。

sentences.en: And yeah, hence the gold coaSt.
sentences.zh: 没错，所以才叫黄金海岸。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So even if the people who will become the Ashanti are being obliged to kind of hand gold over to their superiors, to their masters on the coast, the Denkira,
sentences.zh: 所以，即使那些后来成为阿散蒂人的人被迫向他们的上级，也就是海岸上的主人登基拉人上缴黄金，

sentences.en: they're still getting a bit of it.
sentences.zh: 他们自己还是能留下一部分。

sentences.en: So the fruits of that is starting to percolate back.
sentences.zh: 所以这些成果开始回流。

sentences.en: And basically by the 1670s, they're kind of on the move, but they're still not really ready to make a pitch for independence, still less for conqueSt.
sentences.zh: 基本上到了1670年代，他们开始有所行动，但还没准备好争取独立，更别提征服了。

sentences.en: So in 1680, they have a king who gets killed in battle.
sentences.zh: 所以在1680年，他们的国王在战斗中阵亡了。

sentences.en: And there's a rather sad entry in history that was published in Ghana in the 1970s that said he was buried in an area close to the present day Barclays Bank,
sentences.zh: 20世纪70年代在加纳出版的一部历史著作中有一段相当悲伤的记载，说他被埋葬在靠近现今巴克莱银行的一个区域，

sentences.en: but his head was taken away by the Denkira.
sentences.zh: 但他的头颅被登基拉人带走了。

sentences.en: So that was rather sad.
sentences.zh: 那真是太悲惨了。

sentences.en: And a kind of reminder of the fact that this is a very dangerous world where attempts at rebellion against imperial labor lords are not going to go down well.
sentences.zh: 这也提醒人们，这是一个非常危险的世界，试图反抗帝国劳役领主是不会有好下场的。

sentences.en: Although interestingly, you talked about battles, partly because so much of the areas is, as you said, thick, dense foreSt.
sentences.zh: 虽然有趣的是，你提到了战斗，部分原因正如你所说，大部分地区是茂密、浓密的森林。

sentences.en: Presumably these battles are quite small scale by early modern European standards, are they?
sentences.zh: 据推测，按照近代早期欧洲的标准，这些战斗的规模相当小，是吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But as we will see, that tends to change under the Ashanti.
sentences.zh: 但正如我们将要看到的，在阿散蒂人统治下，这种情况往往会改变。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Who one of their slogans is that they have teeming thousands.
sentences.zh: 他们的口号之一就是他们拥有成千上万的兵力。

sentences.en: So they are very proud of the enormous numbers of warriors that they can call upon.
sentences.zh: 所以他们对能够调动的庞大战士数量感到非常自豪。

sentences.en: Anyway, so the guy who's buried close to Barclays Bank and whose head gets taken away, he was a guy called Abira Yeboah.
sentences.zh: 总之，那个被埋在巴克莱银行附近且头颅被带走的人，名叫阿比拉·耶博阿。

sentences.en: And he has a nephew called Osei Tutu.
sentences.zh: 他有一个侄子叫奥塞·图图。

sentences.en: And he is the guy who is commemorated by the Ashanti as the founder of their greatness.
sentences.zh: 他就是被阿散蒂人纪念为他们伟大事业奠基人的人。

sentences.en: He's Cyrus the Great.
sentences.zh: 他就是居鲁士大帝。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And again, there are kind of echoes of maybe more biblical legends.
sentences.zh: 同样，这里也有一些类似圣经传说的回响。

sentences.en: So the story is that his mother was barren for many, many years, couldn't have a child.
sentences.zh: 故事是说他的母亲多年不孕，无法生育。

sentences.en: And then she goes to the shrine of a very powerful river and prays to the God there.
sentences.zh: 后来她去了一座强大河流的神龛，向那里的神祈祷。

sentences.en: And miraculously, she becomes pregnant.
sentences.zh: 奇迹般地，她怀孕了。

sentences.en: So that's a kind of staple of biblical stories of prophets.
sentences.zh: 这是圣经中先知故事的典型桥段。

sentences.en: So he is given as a hostage to the Denkira.
sentences.zh: 后来他被当作人质送给了登基拉人。

sentences.en: And this is a bit like, I guess, Philip of Macedon going to Thebes.
sentences.zh: 这有点像马其顿的腓力二世去底比斯那样。

sentences.en: You know, he's treated quite well.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他受到了很好的对待。

sentences.en: You know, he's treated as a prince.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他被当作王子对待。

sentences.en: He's brought up, you know, a bit like, I don't know, barbarians going to the court of consent in April.
sentences.zh: 他被抚养长大，就像，我不知道，蛮族被送到君士坦丁堡的宫廷里一样。

sentences.en: He's brought up by the Denkira in their ways.
sentences.zh: 他是在登基拉人的方式下被抚养长大的。

sentences.en: And in fact, he ends up as a shield bearer to the king.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他最终成了国王的持盾者。

sentences.en: So this is a great honor.
sentences.zh: 这是一种巨大的荣誉。

sentences.en: And this clearly gives him the chance to study the way that the Denkira fight.
sentences.zh: 这显然让他有机会研究登基拉人的作战方式。

sentences.en: So he's studying the Denkira way of war.
sentences.zh: 所以他正在研究登基拉人的战争之道。

sentences.en: So it's very Philip of Macedon.
sentences.zh: 这非常像马其顿的腓力二世。

sentences.en: Because Philip studied the Thebes, didn't he?
sentences.zh: 因为腓力研究了底比斯，不是吗？

sentences.en: And used his knowledge.
sentences.zh: 并运用了他的知识。

sentences.en: And that's fascinating.
sentences.zh: 那太令人着迷了。

sentences.en: Or say Arminius, the German auxiliary who ends up wiping out the three legions.
sentences.zh: 或者像阿米尼乌斯，那个最终消灭了三个罗马军团的德国辅助兵。

sentences.en: Avarus.
sentences.zh: 瓦卢斯。

sentences.en: Avarus.
sentences.zh: 瓦卢斯。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So it's a standard kind of imperial technique.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种标准的帝国手段。

sentences.en: And the Denkira are clearly doing it.
sentences.zh: 而登基拉人显然正在这样做。

sentences.en: However, Ossetutu is a naughty boy and he gets embroiled in a sex scandal when one of the princesses gets pregnant.
sentences.zh: 然而，奥塞·图图是个淘气的男孩，当其中一位公主怀孕时，他卷入了一场性丑闻。

sentences.en: There is much to do and he has to run away.
sentences.zh: 事情闹得很大，他不得不逃跑。

sentences.en: So he escapes.
sentences.zh: 于是他逃走了。

sentences.en: And he's now very much on his uppers because he's, you know, he's being hunted by the Denkira.
sentences.zh: 他现在处境非常窘迫，因为他正被登基拉人追捕。

sentences.en: He can't go back.
sentences.zh: 他无法回头了。

sentences.en: He'd take up his princely status.
sentences.zh: 他得承担起王子的身份。

sentences.en: Seems like he's burned his bridges.
sentences.zh: 看来他是破釜沉舟了。

sentences.en: But then he meets a remarkable man called Okompho Anokie.
sentences.zh: 但随后他遇见了一位非凡的人，名叫奥孔福·阿诺基。

sentences.en: So if I'll say Tutu is King Arthur, Okompho Anokie is Merlin.
sentences.zh: 所以如果说图图是亚瑟王，那奥孔福·阿诺基就是梅林。

sentences.en: Or Gandalf.
sentences.zh: 或者是甘道夫。

sentences.en: He is a man who has deep, deep command of magic.
sentences.zh: 他是一个对魔法有着极深造诣的人。

sentences.en: And the story is that he was born with the white tail of a cow in one hand and totem poles in the other.
sentences.zh: 传说他出生时，一只手拿着牛的白尾巴，另一只手拿着图腾柱。

sentences.en: And these are signs of his remarkable destiny.
sentences.zh: 这些都是他非凡命运的征兆。

sentences.en: And it probably won't surprise you to learn that his mother, who had a peculiarly coloured hand, had been executed by the king of Denkira as a witch.
sentences.zh: 你可能不会感到惊讶，他的母亲——那个长着一只颜色奇特的手的女人——曾被登基拉国王以女巫的罪名处决。

sentences.en: She had a peculiarly coloured hand.
sentences.zh: 她长着一只颜色奇特的手。

sentences.en: That's the story.
sentences.zh: 故事就是这样。

sentences.en: That's the story.
sentences.zh: 故事就是这样。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: What was the colour?
sentences.zh: 是什么颜色？

sentences.en: Not sure.
sentences.zh: 不确定。

sentences.en: Maybe a birthmark on her hand?
sentences.zh: 也许是她手上的胎记？

sentences.en: Oh, you and your withering scepticism.
sentences.zh: 噢，你和你那令人扫兴的怀疑态度。

sentences.en: Okay, fine.
sentences.zh: 好吧，行。

sentences.en: I'll just believe it.
sentences.zh: 我就当它是真的吧。

sentences.en: She had a green hand.
sentences.zh: 她长着一只绿色的手。

sentences.en: Let's crack on.
sentences.zh: 我们继续吧。

sentences.en: With his command of deep magic, Ossetutu is able to start thinking, well, I'm going to get my own back on the Denkira.
sentences.zh: 凭借着深厚的魔法造诣，奥塞·图图开始思考：好吧，我要向登基拉人复仇。

sentences.en: And I'm not only going to get my own back, I'm going to take them over.
sentences.zh: 而且我不只是要复仇，我还要征服他们。

sentences.en: And he recognises that to do that, he has to forge a single people out of the many different kind of tribal entities, different villages,
sentences.zh: 他意识到要做到这一点，就必须将森林中散落的众多不同部落实体、不同村庄，

sentences.en: different groupings that are scattered over the foreSt.
sentences.zh: 以及不同的群体，凝聚成一个统一的民族。

sentences.en: And each grouping, the head of each grouping, brilliantly, the marker of his power is a stool.
sentences.zh: 而每个群体的首领，巧妙的是，他们权力的标志是一张凳子。

sentences.en: They're absolute masters of woodwork.
sentences.zh: 他们是绝对的木工大师。

sentences.en: In fact, their craftsmen are sensational.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们的工匠技艺惊人。

sentences.en: And so the stools are often beautifully, you know, the more beautiful the stool, the more prestigious you are.
sentences.zh: 所以凳子通常都很精美，你知道的，凳子越精美，你的地位就越显赫。

sentences.en: But basically, there can be only one.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，只能有一个赢家。

sentences.en: And so a Comfo Inokie burns all the stools of all the, you know, all the various tribal leaders.
sentences.zh: 于是奥孔福·阿诺基烧毁了所有部落首领的凳子。

sentences.en: He incinerates them as a marker that there can be only one.
sentences.zh: 他将它们焚毁，以此作为“只能有一个”的标志。

sentences.en: And then a spectacular miracle.
sentences.zh: 接着出现了壮观的神迹。

sentences.en: There are sacrifices are performed and the blood steams up to the sky.
sentences.zh: 祭祀仪式举行，鲜血蒸腾直冲云霄。

sentences.en: Sacrifices of animals, presumably.
sentences.zh: 想必是动物祭祀。

sentences.en: Well, possibly or possibly not.
sentences.zh: 嗯，可能吧，也可能不是。

sentences.en: We'll come to that later.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后再谈这个。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: The drums quicken and out of the blood of the sacrifices, a black cloud seems to gather.
sentences.zh: 鼓声渐急，从祭祀的鲜血中，似乎汇聚起了一团黑云。

sentences.en: And it's not immediately obvious to people.
sentences.zh: 人们起初并没有立刻察觉。

sentences.en: And then, you know, only a few kind of pointing out saying, what's this cloud?
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道的，只有少数人指着天空说，那是什么云？

sentences.en: And then it gets thicker and thicker and thicker, blacker than a thundercloud.
sentences.zh: 接着它变得越来越厚，越来越浓，比雷雨云还要漆黑。

sentences.en: And then thunder starts to rumble from out of it.
sentences.zh: 随后，云层中开始传出隆隆的雷声。

sentences.en: And then a thick white dust emerges from the cloud and then falling very, very slowly.
sentences.zh: 紧接着，厚重的白尘从云中涌出，非常、非常缓慢地飘落。

sentences.en: Turning like a seed in a breeze, you know, dropping from a tree.
sentences.zh: 像微风中的种子一样旋转，你知道的，从树上掉落下来。

sentences.en: Do you know what descended?
sentences.zh: 你知道降下来的是什么吗？

sentences.en: What appeared?
sentences.zh: 出现了什么？

sentences.en: Is it a stool?
sentences.zh: 是一张凳子吗？

sentences.en: It is a stool, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，那确实是一张凳子。

sentences.en: And it glints with gold.
sentences.zh: 它闪烁着金色的光芒。

sentences.en: And yet it's not entirely made of gold.
sentences.zh: 但它并不完全是由黄金制成的。

sentences.en: So it's an extraordinary thing.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一件非凡的东西。

sentences.en: Because below the gold, it is that there is exquisitely, fabulously carved wood.
sentences.zh: 因为在黄金之下，那是雕刻得极其精美、绝妙的木头。

sentences.en: And it fell slow, you know, like this kind of seed drops, it drops, it drops.
sentences.zh: 它落得很慢，你知道的，就像那种种子掉落一样，它落下，它落下。

sentences.en: And then do you know into whose lap it falls?
sentences.zh: 你知道它落进了谁的怀里吗？

sentences.en: King Arthur.
sentences.zh: 亚瑟王。

sentences.en: Yeah, Osei Tutu falls into his lap.
sentences.zh: 是的，落进了奥塞·图图的怀里。

sentences.en: And this is a sign.
sentences.zh: 这是一个征兆。

sentences.en: And there's no doubt that this happened, right, Tom?
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问这确实发生了，对吧，汤姆？

sentences.en: I mean, this absolutely happened.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这绝对发生了。

sentences.en: This absolutely happened, as also is the next thing that happened.
sentences.zh: 这绝对发生了，接下来的事情也一样。

sentences.en: Because Akum Fonokye takes the stool and he puts it down.
sentences.zh: 因为奥孔福·阿诺基拿起了那张凳子，把它放了下来。

sentences.en: And then he does what I think anyone in this situation would do,
sentences.zh: 然后他做了我认为在这种情况下任何人都会做的事，

sentences.en: which is to get an albino to sit on it.
sentences.zh: 那就是找一个白化病人坐在上面。

sentences.en: Obviously, obviously.
sentences.zh: 显而易见，显而易见。

sentences.en: And the albino man just vanishes.
sentences.zh: 那个白化病人瞬间就消失了。

sentences.en: He just goes, whoosh, like that.
sentences.zh: 他就像那样，嗖的一声不见了。

sentences.en: And he's gone.
sentences.zh: 他消失了。

sentences.en: And he vanished.
sentences.zh: 他消失了。

sentences.en: He vanished.
sentences.zh: 他消失了。

sentences.en: He sat on the stool and vanished.
sentences.zh: 他坐在凳子上，然后消失了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And the reason for this is that he's been swallowed up by the stool and has given the stool his soul.
sentences.zh: 原因是他被凳子吞噬了，并将自己的灵魂赋予了凳子。

sentences.en: So now the stool has a soul.
sentences.zh: 所以现在这张凳子有了灵魂。

sentences.en: Of the albino.
sentences.zh: 那个白化病人的灵魂。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's a bit like the wishing chair in Enid Blyton.
sentences.zh: 这有点像伊妮德·布莱顿书里的那把许愿椅。

sentences.en: That had a soul.
sentences.zh: 那把椅子也有灵魂。

sentences.en: This is now the soul of this new people that has been forged.
sentences.zh: 这现在就是这个新锻造出的民族的灵魂。

sentences.en: Of the people of the nation.
sentences.zh: 这个国家的民族的灵魂。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so the stool is the golden stool.
sentences.zh: 所以这张凳子就是金凳子。

sentences.en: It's called the Sikha Doar Coffee, the golden stool created on a Friday.
sentences.zh: 它被称为“Sikha Doar Coffee”，即周五创造的金凳子。

sentences.en: And so this is now the great – it's more than an emblem because it has this living soul.
sentences.zh: 所以这不仅仅是一个象征，因为它拥有这个活生生的灵魂。

sentences.en: And from that point on, Dominic, no albino man was ever put to death in the Ashanti Empire.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，多米尼克，阿散蒂帝国再也没有处死过任何白化病人。

sentences.en: Oh, that's a nice – oh, that's a nice touch.
sentences.zh: 噢，那真是一个不错的——噢，那真是个不错的举动。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So they've got the golden stool created on a Friday now.
sentences.zh: 所以他们现在有了周五创造的金凳子。

sentences.en: So that's tremendous.
sentences.zh: 这太了不起了。

sentences.en: But now they need a capital.
sentences.zh: 但现在他们需要一个首都。

sentences.en: And so Osei Tutu does this in a very sensible way.
sentences.zh: 于是奥塞·图图用一种非常明智的方式解决了这个问题。

sentences.en: He plants a tree in three locations.
sentences.zh: 他在三个地点各种下了一棵树。

sentences.en: And he waits to see which one is going to grow the fasteSt.
sentences.zh: 然后他等待看哪一棵长得最快。

sentences.en: And the tree that grows the fastest is a place that comes to be called Comarse.
sentences.zh: 长得最快的那棵树所在的地方，后来被称为库马西。

sentences.en: And so this becomes the capital.
sentences.zh: 于是这里成为了首都。

sentences.en: And this is the place that Bauditch will come, who described it in the passage that you first read.
sentences.zh: 这就是鲍迪奇后来到达的地方，他在你刚才读的那段文字中描述过它。

sentences.en: So they've got the stool.
sentences.zh: 所以他们有了凳子。

sentences.en: Now they've got the capital.
sentences.zh: 现在他们有了首都。

sentences.en: Now they need an army.
sentences.zh: 现在他们需要一支军队。

sentences.en: And what happens next is very, very Spartan.
sentences.zh: 接下来发生的事情非常、非常斯巴达式。

sentences.en: So if Osei Tutu is a bit like King Arthur, he's also a bit like Lycurgus, the guy who establishes the Spartan constitution and turns them into a kind of great war machine.
sentences.zh: 如果说奥塞·图图有点像亚瑟王，那他也有一点像莱库古，那个制定了斯巴达宪法并将他们变成一台伟大战争机器的人。

sentences.en: What he does is to drill them and to make them kind of professional.
sentences.zh: 他所做的是对他们进行操练，使他们变得专业化。

sentences.en: Their entire focus is going to be war.
sentences.zh: 他们的全部重心都将是战争。

sentences.en: And because they're drilled, they can kind of maneuver.
sentences.zh: 因为经过操练，他们能够进行机动。

sentences.en: And again, a bit like the Spartans, a bit like the Zulu, they're very, very adept at holding a center and then kind of like the Zulu is called the bullhorn.
sentences.zh: 同样，有点像斯巴达人，有点像祖鲁人，他们非常擅长坚守中心，然后像祖鲁人所谓的“公牛角”战术那样。

sentences.en: Kind of curling around and flanking.
sentences.zh: 绕到侧翼进行包抄。

sentences.en: Enveloping their opponents.
sentences.zh: 包围他们的对手。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And the Ashanti compare their army to a porcupine because, you know, it's kind of bristling with spears.
sentences.zh: 阿散蒂人将他们的军队比作豪猪，因为，你知道的，它浑身长满了长矛。

sentences.en: But also with guns because they are, you know, it's not just spears.
sentences.zh: 但也配备了枪支，因为他们，你知道的，不仅仅是长矛。

sentences.en: It's absolutely guns.
sentences.zh: 绝对有枪。

sentences.en: They're practicing with guns.
sentences.zh: 他们正在练习使用枪支。

sentences.en: They're sourcing guns from the coaSt.
sentences.zh: 他们正从海岸采购枪支。

sentences.en: As I say, are they trading directly with the Portuguese as well?
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，他们也在直接与葡萄牙人贸易吗？

sentences.en: Or do they have to go through their imperial overlords for that?
sentences.zh: 还是他们必须通过他们的帝国霸主来获取？

sentences.en: It's not entirely clear.
sentences.zh: 这一点并不完全清楚。

sentences.en: As I say, I'm not entirely on top of the trade mechanics of this.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，我并不是完全精通这方面的贸易机制。

sentences.en: And I'm not entirely on top of exactly when it is that this war machine becomes fully equipped with rifles.
sentences.zh: 我也不是完全清楚这台战争机器究竟是在什么时候完全装备了步枪。

sentences.en: But basically, Dominic, the key is it's very, very frightening and very, very menacing.
sentences.zh: 但基本上，多米尼克，关键在于它非常、非常可怕，也非常、非常有威胁性。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Essentially, the point comes where they think we're ready to take on the Denkira and to throw the Denkira and yoke off.
sentences.zh: 本质上，当他们认为自己准备好对抗登基拉并摆脱登基拉的枷锁时，时机就到了。

sentences.en: But to begin with, I'm afraid to say it goes very badly for them.
sentences.zh: 但遗憾的是，起初他们的进展非常糟糕。

sentences.en: Fortunately, however, Nokia is able to step in and do his magic stuff.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，诺基亚能够介入并施展他的魔法。

sentences.en: That's good.
sentences.zh: 那很好。

sentences.en: So he uses his magic to secure the defection of various Denkirian generals.
sentences.zh: 所以他利用魔法促使多位登基拉将军倒戈。

sentences.en: So they come over with their troops.
sentences.zh: 于是他们带着部队投诚了。

sentences.en: And the other thing that he does that's very cool is that he turns himself into a vulture and he scatters the body parts of one of their own generals who's fallen in battle.
sentences.zh: 他做的另一件非常酷的事情是，他把自己变成了一只秃鹫，并散布了一位在战斗中阵亡的敌方将军的尸块。

sentences.en: He scatters it all over the enemy.
sentences.zh: 他把尸块散布在敌人身上。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: That would be very off-putting.
sentences.zh: 那会让人非常反感。

sentences.en: Yeah, it is off-putting.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实很反感。

sentences.en: And it's not good for the Denkira and morale at all.
sentences.zh: 这对登基拉人的士气一点好处都没有。

sentences.en: And even more impressively, he shits in the eye of the enemy general.
sentences.zh: 更令人印象深刻的是，他以秃鹫的身份拉屎在敌方将军的眼睛里。

sentences.en: In his capacity as a vulture.
sentences.zh: 以秃鹫的身份。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 我是说，是的，当然。

sentences.en: I mean, he wouldn't.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他确实会这么做。

sentences.en: And so the net effect of this is that at a place called Fayasi, they win a tremendous victory.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切的最终结果是，在一个叫法亚西的地方，他们赢得了巨大的胜利。

sentences.en: They basically wipe out the Denkira.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上消灭了登基拉人。

sentences.en: And the Denkiran king, he was so confident of victory that he wasn't even in the battle.
sentences.zh: 而登基拉国王，他对自己获胜太有信心了，以至于他甚至没有参加战斗。

sentences.en: And he was off playing a kind of chess a bit further back.
sentences.zh: 他当时在后方下棋。

sentences.en: And so he gets captured red-handed.
sentences.zh: 于是他被当场抓获。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And he gets brought before Asai Tutu.
sentences.zh: 他被带到了奥塞·图图面前。

sentences.en: And he behaves very, very well, very bravely.
sentences.zh: 他表现得非常好，非常勇敢。

sentences.en: He embraces, willingly embraces death.
sentences.zh: 他欣然接受了死亡。

sentences.en: And he says, my crown is loSt.
sentences.zh: 他说，我的王冠已失。

sentences.en: My empire is lost because of war.
sentences.zh: 我的帝国因战争而覆灭。

sentences.en: And in the Twi language, Asha means war.
sentences.zh: 在特威语中，Asha 的意思是战争。

sentences.en: And Ti apparently means because of.
sentences.zh: 而 Ti 显然是“因为”的意思。

sentences.en: I'm not pretending I am in any way familiar with the Twi language.
sentences.zh: 我并不是假装自己对特威语有多熟悉。

sentences.en: If you have any Ghanaian listeners, I apologize for my...
sentences.zh: 如果你们有加纳听众，我为我的……表示歉意。

sentences.en: How does it compare with your Portuguese, Tom?

sentences.zh: 因此，所有的那些权杖、宝剑、黄金胸饰等等，你知道，这些都不是随机选择的。

sentences.en: They are as significant as similar such things would be in, say, in a Byzantine court.
sentences.zh: 这就是鲍迪奇和英国人在19世纪初所遇到的非凡文明。

sentences.zh: 所以反驳的观点，我的意思是，最著名的例子就是大卫·利文斯通，对吧？

sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So it's sort of people, even if we might regard it now as hypocritical, they at the time want to believe in a civilizing mission.
sentences.zh: 所以，即使我们现在可能认为这很虚伪，但当时的人们确实想要相信一种文明使命。

sentences.en: I suppose that's true, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我想那是真的，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean.
sentences.zh: 我是说。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, they don't regard it themselves as pure hypocrisy, do they?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们自己并不认为这是纯粹的虚伪，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, no, they don't regard it as hypocrisy.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不，他们不认为这是虚伪。

sentences.en: They regard slavery as an evil and that they see it as their mission to stamp it out.
sentences.zh: 他们视奴隶制为邪恶，并将消除它视为自己的使命。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And that's definitely, I mean, it's not just hypocrisy.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是，我的意思是，这不仅仅是虚伪。

sentences.en: I mean, it's not just a kind of cover.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这不仅仅是一种掩饰。

sentences.en: They passionately believe it.
sentences.zh: 他们是充满激情地相信这一点。

sentences.en: And an example of this is a man called Sir Charles McCarthy, who is the governor of the British territories along the Gold CoaSt.
sentences.zh: 一个例子就是查尔斯·麦卡锡爵士，他是黄金海岸沿岸英国领地的总督。

sentences.en: And he's an interesting, so he's actually Franco-Irish.
sentences.zh: 他是个有趣的人，实际上他是法裔爱尔兰人。

sentences.en: So he's, I think his father was a French emigre from the Russian Revolution and his mother, Dominic, was from Cork.
sentences.zh: 所以，我想他的父亲是法国大革命时期的流亡者，而他的母亲多米尼克来自科克。

sentences.en: So very good, very good stock there.
sentences.zh: 所以，出身非常好，非常好的血统。

sentences.en: And he's a very, very keen abolitioniSt.
sentences.zh: 而且他是一位非常、非常热心的废奴主义者。

sentences.en: He corresponds with Wilberforce.
sentences.zh: 他与威伯福斯有通信往来。

sentences.en: He's very into all of that.
sentences.zh: 他非常热衷于这一切。

sentences.en: And he feels that what the Ashanti are getting up to is very poor form.
sentences.zh: 他觉得阿散蒂人的所作所为非常糟糕。

sentences.en: And so in 1823, he launches an expedition against them, but he doesn't take as many people as he should because he's complacent and overconfident.
sentences.zh: 因此在1823年，他发动了一场针对他们的远征，但他带的人没有应有的那么多，因为他自满且过度自信。

sentences.en: And at a place called Nesaman Kau, I hope I pronounced that right, he gets ambushed and his head gets chopped off and his skull gets taken to Kamasi.
sentences.zh: 在一个叫内萨曼考的地方，希望我发音正确，他遭到了伏击，头被砍了下来，头骨被带到了库马西。

sentences.en: And it's lined with gold and it's used as a drinking cup.
sentences.zh: 它被镶上金边，用作饮酒杯。

sentences.en: It so often happens in history, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 历史上经常发生这种情况，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, I'm thinking about all kinds of Bulgars and, you know, it's a very petchenegg behavior.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我想到各种保加尔人，你知道，这是一种非常佩切涅格人的行为。

sentences.en: Very petchenegg behavior.
sentences.zh: 非常佩切涅格人的行为。

sentences.en: Yes, it's very, very, very petchenegg behavior.
sentences.zh: 是的，这非常、非常、非常佩切涅格人的行为。

sentences.en: So that hasn't gone well.
sentences.zh: 所以那次行动并不顺利。

sentences.en: But then it's the Ashanti's turn to underestimate the British because they then attack the Gold Coast,
sentences.zh: 但随后轮到阿散蒂人低估英国人了，因为他们随后袭击了黄金海岸，

sentences.en: wanting to get rid of the Europeans altogether so that they can control the whole trade.
sentences.zh: 想要彻底摆脱欧洲人，以便他们能控制整个贸易。

sentences.en: The British managed to stave off the attack with the help of the Denkira.
sentences.zh: 英国人在登基拉人的帮助下成功抵御了这次袭击。

sentences.en: So there's a kind of tug of war now between the British and the Ashanti over who is going to be the preponderant imperial power.
sentences.zh: 所以现在英国人和阿散蒂人之间进行了一场拉锯战，看谁将成为占主导地位的帝国力量。

sentences.en: And the Denkira have decided that they'd rather side with the British than with the Ashanti.
sentences.zh: 而登基拉人决定他们宁愿站在英国人一边，也不愿站在阿散蒂人一边。

sentences.en: And so by 1826, the British are able to basically to force the Ashanti to a score draw.
sentences.zh: 因此到了1826年，英国人基本上能够迫使阿散蒂人打成平手。

sentences.en: And they do this with the help of Congreve rockets, which are now kind of in their heyday and nothing that the Ashanti have seen before.
sentences.zh: 他们是在康格里夫火箭的帮助下做到这一点的，这种火箭当时正处于鼎盛时期，是阿散蒂人以前从未见过的。

sentences.en: And so they establish a river is kind of established as the markers between the two empires.
sentences.zh: 于是他们建立了一条河流作为两个帝国之间的分界线。

sentences.en: And in 1831, that is confirmed as the border.
sentences.zh: 1831年，这被确认为边界。

sentences.en: And then over the course of the 19th century, it's trade and war.
sentences.zh: 然后在整个19世纪，这就是贸易与战争并存。

sentences.en: So the British do start to supply the Ashanti with the kind of the appurtenances of industrial civilization.
sentences.zh: 所以英国人确实开始向阿散蒂人提供工业文明的各种附属品。

sentences.en: And because the Ashanti are status obsessed, all these appurtenances take on tremendous kind of significance.
sentences.zh: 而且因为阿散蒂人痴迷于地位，所有这些附属品都具有了巨大的意义。

sentences.en: They'll even have carriages.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至会有马车。

sentences.en: There are no horses, but they'll get people to kind of draw them.
sentences.zh: 虽然没有马，但他们会让人拉着走。

sentences.en: And there's a British observer who describes going into the Stain Palace and having a look and saying that it's a bit like a gentleman's club,
sentences.zh: 有一位英国观察员描述说，走进斯坦宫殿看了一眼，说它有点像绅士俱乐部，

sentences.en: that there are copies of the Times kind of scattered around.
sentences.zh: 到处散落着《泰晤士报》的副本。

sentences.en: That seems so strange.
sentences.zh: 这看起来太奇怪了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So it's a kind of curious mix.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种奇怪的组合。

sentences.en: But at the same time that trade is going on, wars are being fought.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，贸易在进行，战争也在打。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And over the course of the 19th century, there are actually four more wars.
sentences.zh: 在整个19世纪，实际上又发生了四次战争。

sentences.en: And it's the last three that are really devastating for the Ashanti.
sentences.zh: 最后三次对阿散蒂人来说确实是毁灭性的。

sentences.en: Because by this point, Britain is at its imperial industrial heyday.
sentences.zh: 因为到这个时候，英国正处于其帝国工业的鼎盛时期。

sentences.en: And really, the balance of power has shifted so dramatically in the favor of the British.
sentences.zh: 而且，力量平衡已经戏剧性地向英国人倾斜。

sentences.en: And the Ashanti don't really understand this.
sentences.zh: 而阿散蒂人并不真正理解这一点。

sentences.en: They don't really appreciate this.
sentences.zh: 他们并不真正意识到这一点。

sentences.en: Because I think the Ashanti see the British as both perfidious and cowardly.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为阿散蒂人视英国人为背信弃义且懦弱的。

sentences.en: And the British see the Ashanti as kind of just terrifying savages who need to be tamed.
sentences.zh: 而英国人视阿散蒂人为需要被驯服的恐怖野蛮人。

sentences.en: And neither characterization is a fair one.
sentences.zh: 这两种描述都不公平。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But by 1872, the Ashanti are still doing this kind of, oh, let's go off and raid the Gold Coast and see if we can, you know, conquer it.
sentences.zh: 但到了1872年，阿散蒂人仍然在做这种事，哦，让我们去突袭黄金海岸，看看我们能不能，你知道，征服它。

sentences.en: And this is a foodish thing to be doing in 1872.
sentences.zh: 在1872年做这种事真是愚蠢。

sentences.en: And so they abortive attack, they get beaten off, and they steal some missionaries and take them off.
sentences.zh: 所以他们那次袭击失败了，被击退了，他们还绑架了一些传教士带走。

sentences.en: And the guy who is in charge of reprisals is a man called Sir Garnet Wolseley.
sentences.zh: 负责报复行动的人是一个叫加内特·沃尔斯利爵士的人。

sentences.en: I mean, an enormously Victorian general.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，一位非常典型的维多利亚时代将军。

sentences.en: I mean, the essence of a Victorian general.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，维多利亚时代将军的精髓。

sentences.en: The moustache, the ramrod back.
sentences.zh: 那胡子，那挺直的脊梁。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Sir Garnet Wolseley, I mean, an absolutely towering figure in Victorian popular culture.
sentences.zh: 加内特·沃尔斯利爵士，我的意思是，维多利亚时代流行文化中绝对的高大人物。

sentences.en: And actually, Tom, you know, Henry Morton Stanley, as in Dr. Livingston, he covered the third Anglo-Oshanty War as a war correspondent.
sentences.zh: 实际上，汤姆，你知道，亨利·莫顿·斯坦利，就是那个寻找利文斯通博士的，他作为战地记者报道了第三次英阿战争。

sentences.en: So I suppose it's the 1870s.
sentences.zh: 所以我猜那是19世纪70年代。

sentences.en: And by that time, you know, Britain has really, imperialism has become kind of pop culture in a way.
sentences.zh: 到那时，你知道，英国确实，帝国主义在某种程度上已经成为流行文化了。

sentences.en: It has.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And so the whole thing is done as a kind of exemplary.
sentences.zh: 所以整个事情被当作一个典范来处理。

sentences.en: It's like a story.
sentences.zh: 就像一个故事。

sentences.en: And Wolse is aware the whole way through that the eyes of Britain are upon him.
sentences.zh: 沃尔斯利全程都知道英国的目光注视着他。

sentences.en: And so he is kind of behaving like the hero of an exemplary military tale.
sentences.zh: 所以他的行为就像一个模范军事故事中的英雄。

sentences.en: So he sends an ultimatum to the Ashanti by traction engine.
sentences.zh: 于是他用牵引机给阿散蒂人发了最后通牒。

sentences.en: By traction engine.
sentences.zh: 用牵引机。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a tremendous thing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这真是件了不起的事。

sentences.en: And the Ashanti are hugely unimpressed by it, it has to be said.
sentences.zh: 必须说，阿散蒂人对此印象极其深刻，但并不是好的那种。

sentences.en: And they reject the ultimatum.
sentences.zh: 他们拒绝了最后通牒。

sentences.en: And so Wolseley prepares for battle.
sentences.zh: 于是沃尔斯利准备战斗。

sentences.en: And in James Morris' accounts of this war, he has my favorite ever footnote.
sentences.zh: 在詹姆斯·莫里斯对这场战争的记述中，他有我最喜欢的脚注。

sentences.en: So he says, Sir Garnett was quite certain of victory, but was resigned to the possibility of casualties, soldiers being made to die in action.
sentences.zh: 他说，加内特爵士对胜利很有把握，但对可能出现的伤亡，即士兵在战斗中阵亡的情况，也做好了心理准备。

sentences.en: And oh, Sir Garnett wrote, how fortunate they are who do so.
sentences.zh: 哦，加内特爵士写道，那些这样做的人是多么幸运啊。

sentences.en: To which Morris attaches this footnote.
sentences.zh: 莫里斯对此加了这样一个脚注。

sentences.en: In the event only 18 had the good luck to be killed, the 55 enjoyed the consolation of dying from disease.
sentences.zh: 结果只有18人有幸阵亡，55人享受了死于疾病的慰藉。

sentences.en: So, so it's, it's, it, and as that implies, it's a route.
sentences.zh: 所以，所以，这，正如那所暗示的，这是一场溃败。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The, the, the, the, the king flees Camarcy, his noblemen flee it.
sentences.zh: 国王逃离了库马西，他的贵族们也逃离了。

sentences.en: Wolseley enters the city and it, you know, is hugely impressed by it.
sentences.zh: 沃尔斯利进入了这座城市，你知道，对它印象非常深刻。

sentences.en: Very, very struck by the sophistication of the architecture, the, you know, the cleanliness of the streets, all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 对建筑的精致、街道的整洁等等印象非常深刻。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: However, there is also a lot that he is appalled by.
sentences.zh: 然而，也有很多让他感到震惊的东西。

sentences.en: And there's a brilliant account.
sentences.zh: 有一个精彩的记述。

sentences.en: So I will, I will read some of the, the descriptions of what he found.
sentences.zh: 所以我将读一些关于他所发现的东西的描述。

sentences.en: And so he found, it is reported, the great death drum decorated with human skulls and thigh bones.
sentences.zh: 据报道，他发现了装饰着人类头骨和大腿骨的伟大死亡之鼓。

sentences.en: The stools that had belonged to the king's ancestors stood near it.
sentences.zh: 属于国王祖先的凳子就立在它旁边。

sentences.en: And then outside the palace, this account claims another spot that was visited was the death grove,
sentences.zh: 然后在宫殿外，这个记述声称另一个被参观的地方是死亡之林，

sentences.en: a gruesome hollow in the center of a clump of trees and tall reeds into which the bodies of the victims of human sacrifice were thrown.
sentences.zh: 那是树丛和高大芦苇丛中心的一个阴森的凹地，人祭受害者的尸体被扔进那里。

sentences.en: It was now nearly filled with their remains.
sentences.zh: 现在它几乎被他们的遗骸填满了。

sentences.en: So some people argue very bitterly about this now, don't they?
sentences.zh: 所以现在有些人对此争论得非常激烈，不是吗？

sentences.en: They do.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Because some people, some people say, well, this gives the light, the idea that the British were just evil, militaristic bullies.
sentences.zh: 因为有些人说，这反驳了英国人只是邪恶的、军国主义的恶霸这一观点。

sentences.en: And actually the Ashanti weren't, you know, they weren't kindly social workers.
sentences.zh: 实际上阿散蒂人也不是，你知道，他们不是善良的社会工作者。

sentences.en: And, and, and we shouldn't present this in sort of moralistic good and evil terms in which the British are the bad guys because they're imperialists.
sentences.zh: 我们不应该用道德上的善恶术语来呈现这一点，即英国人是坏人，因为他们是帝国主义者。

sentences.en: And then other people say, oh, but these accounts of the Ashanti are, you know, are loaded with, with prejudice.
sentences.zh: 然后其他人说，哦，但这些关于阿散蒂人的记述充满了偏见。

sentences.en: And actually the, this is all nonsense and the British were making all this stuff up.
sentences.zh: 实际上，这全是胡说八道，英国人编造了所有这些东西。

sentences.en: Is there any, do you have any sense of where the, right?
sentences.zh: 你对这方面有什么了解吗，对吧？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Maybe they are.
sentences.zh: 也许他们是。

sentences.en: I mean, as I say, I, I said earlier, I'm, I'm not aware of the latest academic thinking on this, but these are two empires and empires are founded on violence.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，正如我刚才说的，我不知道对此最新的学术看法，但这是两个帝国，而帝国是建立在暴力之上的。

sentences.en: And, you know, the British are more effective in their violence, but the Ashanti definitely, you know, I mean, the whole, you know,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，英国人在暴力方面更有效，但阿散蒂人绝对，你知道，我的意思是，整个，你知道，

sentences.en: they wouldn't have this empire unless they were very violent and intimidating.
sentences.zh: 如果他们不非常暴力和具有威慑力，他们就不会有这个帝国。

sentences.en: It's, you know, that's the way empires are.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就是帝国的运作方式。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And, and, and we'll see is, is appalled by, I mean, he was certainly, he, he is sufficiently appalled by what he finds there to blow it all up.
sentences.zh: 而且，沃尔斯利对，我的意思是，他确实对他在那里发现的东西感到足够震惊，以至于把一切都炸毁了。

sentences.en: So yeah, he lays depth charges and then he retreats and the whole thing gets blown up.
sentences.zh: 所以是的，他安放了深水炸弹，然后撤退，整个地方都被炸毁了。

sentences.en: So, I mean, maybe it's just a random act of vandalism.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，也许这只是一种随机的破坏行为。

sentences.en: I would have thought it's unlikely.
sentences.zh: 我认为不太可能。

sentences.en: I mean, it is definitely vandalism, but I wouldn't thought he'd do it just for the fun of it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这绝对是破坏行为，但我认为他不会仅仅为了好玩而这样做。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Maybe he did.
sentences.zh: 也许他确实是。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I'm, I'm very open to being corrected on this by people who know more.
sentences.zh: 如果有人比我更了解这一点，我非常乐意接受指正。

sentences.en: I mean, the truth, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 我是说，真相，我想。

sentences.en: The truth is when this is absolutely one of those stories, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 真相是，这绝对是那种典型的故事之一，不是吗？

sentences.en: One of these stories of 19th century imperialism that people look at it through tinted spectacles that reflect their own political prejudices.
sentences.zh: 这是那种十九世纪帝国主义的故事之一，人们透过带有色眼镜去看待它，而这些眼镜反映了他们自己的政治偏见。

sentences.en: Well, I, I mean, I think there's a case for saying that perhaps, you know, I talked about how the, the British and the Ashanti don't really understand each other.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我是说，我认为有理由说，也许，你知道，我谈到了英国人和阿散蒂人之间并不真正了解彼此。

sentences.en: But on another level, you might say, actually, perhaps they, they, they understand each other better than we are qualified to do now, because we are so instinctively anti-imperial.
sentences.zh: 但在另一个层面上，你可能会说，实际上，也许他们比我们现在有资格去评判的要更了解彼此，因为我们本能地反帝国主义。

sentences.en: You know, Wolsey admires the Ashanti as an imperial people.
sentences.zh: 你知道，沃尔斯利（Wolsey）作为帝国的一员，很钦佩阿散蒂人。

sentences.en: He admires their discipline.
sentences.zh: 他钦佩他们的纪律。

sentences.en: He admires their, their courage.
sentences.zh: 他钦佩他们的勇气。

sentences.en: He admires their character.
sentences.zh: 他钦佩他们的品格。

sentences.en: He recognizes them, you know, rather like the British recognize the Zulus as worthy adversaries.
sentences.zh: 他认可他们，你知道，就像英国人认可祖鲁人是值得尊敬的对手一样。

sentences.en: But he is also sufficiently self-confident in his own morality and in the morality of the empire that he represents for it never to cross his mind that blowing up, you know, the,
sentences.zh: 但他对自己所代表的道德以及帝国的道德也足够自信，以至于他从未想过，炸毁，你知道，

sentences.en: the, the sacred capital of, of, of a people might in any way perhaps be kind of echoing the very behavior that he's condemning.
